decision_scope: Complete a source-bounded proposal selection; defer executable adapter admission and retain the pinned engine as a reference.
preferred_proposal_route: Pinned R original-language wrapper, supplied fully observed directed acyclic graph, single exposure/outcome, total-effect adjustment

identity.alias_boundary: Interfaces share a core but have distinct wrappers, build inputs and precondition behavior; they are not independent discovery engines.

license.underscore_helpers: MIT declarations at selected1.8.3 and1.13.1 files
license.interpretation: Preserve applicable notices and actual corresponding-source/distribution duties; a subprocess or browser boundary alone is not a license exemption.

dependencies.boundary: Do not mix browser/Node/R generated artifacts or borrow the test dependency range as a production lock.

maintenance.comment: README reports infrequent CRAN updates; this is an historical author statement, not a verified current maintenance conclusion.

target_and_uncertainty: Graphical adjustment for a supplied causal graph and declared total-effect query. No automatic discovery, fitted effect, calibrated graph/effect uncertainty or verified causal premises.
reason: The pinned shared core, original license and direct dependency/build/wrapper declarations support a concrete proposal route without prior bank or prototype evidence.
A narrow original-language wrapper avoids assuming that an implementation port preserves adjustment semantics; no measured embedding need justifies a port now.
R query checks are stronger than the selected raw JavaScript boolean boundary for missing endpoints. The chosen wrapper and future native comparisons must be explicit.
General graph-class and ambiguity-removing transformations exceed the preferred initial profile. Keep graph authoring and analyst approval separate from identification and estimation.
Deferring executable admission is a prototype obligation, not a reason to block other proposal research or declare this proposal choice unresolved.

alternatives.route: Unrestricted adoption of GUI, R and all graph classes
alternatives.reason: Distinct wrappers, graph validation limits and unsupported estimands would share an unjustified blanket guarantee.
Would duplicate parser, graph, algorithm and regression obligations without a demonstrated deployment constraint.

alternatives.route: Pinned direct Node or local browser use
alternatives.reason: Requires its own artifact loading, dependency, error and data-flow review. Default remote graph save/load must not be assumed local.
Some identifiable effects lack an adjustment formula. Each engine has its own graph/input completeness and failure contract.

alternatives.route: Human-reviewed explicit DAG and transparent small oracle
alternatives.reason: Makes premises and invalid conditioning visible while claiming no automatic graph truth.

costs_to_measure: Pinned R/V8 and generated JS build retention
Enumeration growth, startup, latency and memory including failed requests
Complete notices and transitive dependency inventory
Separate estimation, support and uncertainty qualification

owner_obligations.scientific_owner: Own the graph assumptions, total-effect estimand, time ordering, selected covariates, positivity and interpretation of refusal.
owner_obligations.adapter_maintainer: Own the exact wrapper/generated artifacts, lockfile, typed query checks, truncation and failure distinctions, and native conformance.
owner_obligations.product_rights_owner: Review the actual dependency/distribution path and third-party notices before admitting executable reuse.

revisit_trigger: Acquire and bind the complete selected R/V8/generated-core distribution and dependency/notice inventory; compare native valid-empty-set, confounding, collider, mediator, invalid names/query, cycles, capped enumeration, parse errors and resource failures against the declared contract. A new revision, graph class, wrapper or deployment arrangement reopens review.

evidence.anchor: Fourteen authenticated blobs and bounded primary-source claims
Three independent exact SCM oracles; no native execution
Proposed selected conversion and failure contract
Preserved DNS failure before successful authorized fixed-collector retry
Exact source checks and authored reference computation

limitations: Fourteen authentic selected files and a complete tree support a bounded proposal selection, not a complete distribution, resolved executable environment or transitive-rights inventory.
Root GPLv2 text, R GPL-2 declaration, a GPL2-or-later file header and MIT helper declarations retain their own scopes; blanket rights for a specific product arrangement are not inferred.
Two vendored Underscore versions and a third test dependency range are distinct observations. Their presence alone proves no version vulnerability, runtime loading path or interchangeability.
No browser, Node, R or upstream test execution; no adapter permission, effect estimate, confidence guarantee, graph discovery or verified bank causal premises.
The selected commit is dated2024 and R DESCRIPTION dated2023. These establish historical identity, not present maintenance capacity or a support contract.
This new reuse record is program evidence; its additional source findings are not yet merged into a successor of the current1068-page monograph.
